thought.text: The seed doesn't set the fork's custom GDPR consent fields. Let me add them.

reasoning_content:
So the acceptance validator defines attr_readers/writers for `terms_data_storage` etc. So seed needs to set them to "1". The seed's create_user sets `terms_of_service: "1"` but not the custom terms. Since the fork's custom validations require terms_data_storage/protection/general, we need to set them in the seed. But wait — maybe guest? The seeds might rely on system user? Let me check whether `guest?` returns true. Actually `unless: :guest?` only for data_storage. Others apply always.

The upstream (hanuschka) repo would have its own seeds that set these. This fork's dev_seeds/users.rb was likely not updated. Let me check the fork seed again — it only sets terms_of_service. So the correct fix is to add terms_data_storage/protection/general to the seed create_user.

But careful - modifying seed files. This is an installation adaptation. Let me add them.

Actually wait, maybe the intended behavior: these validations only run `on: :create`. Both forks. Hmm. The admin fork clearly customized user model with German validations, and their dev seeds may be different. Let me check the opencode repo's users.rb at the branch cli_wur_2... but we have it locally — it's the same file we have. So indeed the seed is inconsistent.

Let me just add the three terms to the seed. This is the minimal fix to get seeding to work.

action.command:
cd /workspace; python3 - <<'PY'
p="db/dev_seeds/users.rb"
s=open(p).read()
old='      terms_of_service:       "1",\n'
new='      terms_of_service:       "1",\n      terms_data_storage:     "1",\n      terms_data_protection:  "1",\n      terms_general:          "1",\n'
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,"w").write(s)
print("patched")
PY
sed -n '1,15p' db/dev_seeds/users.rb
